executive_summary: The Docker environment for the ICS lab exhibits multiple critical security weaknesses. Seven containers have exposed services with high-severity image vulnerabilities (e.g., WireGuard, VNC, web interfaces) that could be exploited to compromise ICS components. Elevated capabilities (CAP_NET_ADMIN) in five containers enable network manipulation, while four containers run as root with no resource limits, increasing availability risks. Attacker tools (Caldera, Kali) are co-located with ICS components in the DMZ network, creating lateral movement pathways. Immediate remediation is required to prevent remote exploitation of critical infrastructure.

findings.title: Elevated Network Capabilities
findings.explanation: CAP_NET_ADMIN and CAP_NET_RAW allow manipulation of network interfaces and raw socket access, increasing risk of network-based attacks on ICS systems.
findings.remediation: Remove CapAdd or replace with least-privilege capabilities. Use AppArmor/SELinux profiles to restrict network operations.

findings.title: Exposed ICS Network Services
findings.explanation: Published port 51820/udp (WireGuard) with 5 critical and 190+ high vulnerabilities in the image could allow remote exploitation of ICS network infrastructure.
findings.remediation: Remove unnecessary port exposure. Update image to patched version if available. Isolate ICS network from DMZ with network segmentation.

findings.title: Missing Resource Limits
findings.explanation: Unlimited CPU and memory access could allow resource exhaustion attacks disrupting ICS network routing functions.
findings.remediation: Set memory and CPU limits in Docker Compose. Example: mem_limit: 512m, cpu_shares: 512

findings.title: Elevated Network Capabilities
findings.explanation: CAP_NET_ADMIN allows network interface manipulation, increasing risk of ICS network disruption or eavesdropping.
findings.remediation: Remove CapAdd unless explicitly required. Use network policies to restrict traffic.

findings.title: Running as Root User
findings.explanation: Root privileges in ICS workstations increase risk of privilege escalation to critical systems.
findings.remediation: Run container as non-root user. Set user: 'engineer' in Docker Compose.

findings.title: Docker Socket Mount
findings.explanation: Mounting the Docker socket allows container to control the Docker daemon, enabling container escape and arbitrary container creation.
findings.remediation: Remove the Docker socket mount unless absolutely required. Use Docker-in-Docker (dind) or other secure alternatives if needed.

recommendations: Remove all unnecessary port exposures (e.g., 51820/udp, 6080/tcp, 8080/tcp) to limit attack surface
Update all container images to patched versions (e.g., fortiphyd/grfics-router, grfics-scadalts) or rebuild with updated dependencies
Replace elevated capabilities (CAP_NET_ADMIN) with AppArmor/SELinux profiles for least-privilege access
Set memory and CPU limits for all containers (e.g., mem_limit: 1g, cpu_shares: 512) to prevent resource exhaustion
Run containers as non-root users (e.g., user: 'ics_user') to reduce privilege escalation risks
Isolate attacker tools (Caldera, Kali) in a dedicated network with no access to ICS components
limitations: Cannot verify stopped containers or historical configurations
Some vulnerabilities have no available fixes (e.g., CVE-2022-23305 in log4j)
Network segmentation policies cannot be verified without inspecting firewall rules
